the hydroxypropoxy substituent in the platinum(II)-salphen complex has an effect on the DNA binding mode and interactions with the duplex DNA.
the synthesized platinum(II) complexes have a high affinity for DNA.
the hydroxyl functionalization of platinum(II) complexes with salphen ligands has been shown to be effective in improving DNA binding and DNA sensing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structural characterization of the Pt(III) complexes and their interactions with DNA.
the synthesis, characterization and DNA binding studies of hydroxy functionalized platinum(II) complexes and their application in DNA biosensors.
the design of a new series of platinum(II) complexes with hydroxyl functional side chains and their interaction with DNA.

the Pt(II)-salphen complex (3) is a promising optical DNA biosensor with the capability to detect porcine DNA at low concentration (0.5 μM) and with good sensitivity.
hydroxy side chains in Pt(II) salphens can affect their binding affinity and selectivity towards DNA.
the hydroxypropoxy substituent has a significant effect on the binding affinity and selectivity of the platinum(III) complex to DNA.

the hydroxyl functionalization of the platinum( II) salphen complex has been successfully achieved.
the presence of hydroxyl substituents in Pt(II) salphens complexes can affect their spectral properties and DNA binding behaviors.
the Pt(II)-salphen complexes are promising candidates for the development of new anticancer agents.

the presence of hydroxypropoxy substituent on the Pt(II)-salphen complex (3) is a good choice for the application of these complexes as optical DNA biosensor.
the hydroxypropoxy substituent in the Pt(II)-complex (3) can act as a potential DNA biosensor.
